title: 0xf340 — initVRF Missing Access Control Analysis
root_cause: No access control on `initVRF` function, allowing attacker to set an arbitrary address in storage and drain LINK tokens
steps: no access control → vrfRecipient = attacker address
other_code:
Attacker
  │
  ├─[1]─▶ calls victim.initVRF(attacker, LINK)
  │         └─ no access control → vrfRecipient = attacker address
  │
  ├─[2]─▶ for (i = 0; i < 80; i++)
  │           calls victim.call(0x607d60e6, 0)
  │           └─ each call transfers LINK to the attacker
  │
  ├─[3]─▶ after 80 iterations, all LINK fully drained
  │
  ├─[4]─▶ swaps LINK for ETH via UniswapV2
  │
  └─[5]─▶ nets ~4,000 USD worth of ETH
